title: FlashPaged kernel switchpoint analysis
body:
Summary:

This doc captures an investigation into 'kernel switchpoints' in the serving runtime — the heuristics and runtime decisions that switch between FlashAttention, paged-attention, and fused-op paths. Over the last two quarters we've seen intermittent latency regressions at specific sequence length / batch size combinations even though aggregate throughput and median latency look fine. Objective: reproduce the switchpoint behavior, characterize performance cliff regions, and propose changes to selection heuristics and telemetry to prevent regressions in production.

Background and motivation:
- Runtime currently picks an attention kernel based on (model_family, seq_len, batch_size, quant_mode, hw_capabilities).
- FlashAttention is default for short-to-medium seq_len on modern tensor cores. Paged-attention is chosen for long sequences or when memory fragmentation would otherwise lead to OOM. Fused ops selected when operator fusion path triggers for small batches.
- We observed p95 spikes for chat workloads around seq_len=380-420 and batch_size=4 on A100-40GB pools; p50 unaffected. Logs show kernel transitions at these points.

Hypotheses:
1) Sharp performance cliffs occur when kernel selection switches from a single-token-optimized Flash kernel to a tiled/paged kernel where stitching or page boundary handling adds per-token overhead; hysteresis is insufficient so small input perturbations flip kernel choice frequently.
2) Fused-op path selection is overly eager for micro-batches leading to vectorization inefficiencies when combined with KV-cache sizes for long contexts.
3) Quantized kernels (int8/4bit) have different switching thresholds; current heuristics don't account for increased memory pressure and kernel launching overhead.

Microbench setup:
- Hardware: A100-40GB, H100-80GB (single-GPU isolated tests), and a 4×A100 multi-GPU host for multi-GPU scheduling tests.
- Model: rw-large-7B (decoder-only), rw-medium-3B as control.
- Builds: latest master with profiling hooks (PR #842 applied) and a backfilled binary from 2025-08 as baseline.
- Metrics captured: per-kernel call time, per-token latency, p50/p95/p99, kernel-launch overhead, GPU SM utilization, memory alloc/free counts, fragmentation estimates, and profiler traces (Nsight and internal tracing).
- Test matrix: seq_len in {128,256,320,360,380,400,420,512}; batch_size in {1,2,4,8}; quant_mode in {fp16, int8}; KV-cache warm/cold. 3 runs per cell, 2000 requests steady-state plus warmup.

Key observations:
- Switch region: For A100+rw-large-7B+fp16 at batch_size=4, the runtime flips from Flash to paged at seq_len=384. At seq_len=380 Flash is used and p95=34ms, at seq_len=392 paged used and p95=78ms. The transition window is narrow (~12 tokens) and causes requests that land near the boundary to occasionally exceed 200ms.
- Kernel launch overhead: paged-attention path launches multiple kernels with synchronization (cudaStreamSynchronize placed in implementation) resulting in 8–12ms extra per call compared to Flash which consolidates ops.
- Fragmentation/OOM guard: paged kernel reduces peak memory but we rarely hit OOM in these tests; the switch is conservative and seems to be triggered by a heuristic using estimated working set that overestimates by ~10% in common cases.
- Fused ops: For small batches (1–2), fused ops are still good; for batch_size≥4 they sometimes lead to suboptimal warp utilization when combined with the paged path because the internal tiling doesn't align with coalesced loads.
- Quantized modes: int8 paths moved the switchpoint to lower seq_len (~360) because the estimated memory savings are misapplied to kernel selection logic — the runtime assumes int8 always reduces memory pressure enough to prefer a fused/paged fallback, but actual quantized kernels have larger kernel-launch overhead.

Reproduction notes (how to reproduce locally):
1) Checkout PR/branch with extra tracing (runtime branch: attn-switchpoint-telemetry).
2) Run bench script: tools/bench/attn_switchpoint.py --model rw-large-7B --device a100 --seq-start 360 --seq-end 420 --batch 4 --quant fp16 --log-traces s3://redwood-bench/flashpaged/
3) Inspect runtime trace (trace_id printed at run end), grep for KERNEL_SELECT decisions and per-kernel durations.

Root-cause analysis:
- The selection heuristic is a combination of: estimated_alloc = base_alloc + seq_len * kv_entry_size * layers; if estimated_alloc > threshold then choose paged. The constants for kv_entry_size are tuned to worst-case model configs, not observed run-time layout.
- There is no hysteresis: a single request with slightly larger seq_len flips the policy for that request, causing inconsistent p95 across identical workloads.
- Paged-attention path includes additional synchronization points introduced in the paged-implementation refactor (2025-06) which were not present in the original fused code; those adds 6–12ms that dominate p95 when batch_sizes are moderate.

Recommendations (short-term):
- Lower sensitivity: introduce a 10% hysteresis window and prefer the lower-latency kernel when estimated_alloc is within ±10% of threshold.
- Telemetry: emit kernel-selection event with (seq_len, batch_size, model_family, chosen_kernel, estimated_alloc, actual_alloc) to Sentry/metrics for postmortems. Instrument percent of requests that flip kernels.
- Remove unnecessary cudaStreamSynchronize calls in paged-attention path (PR candidate: runtime#859). Replace with event-based ordering or fine-grained stream dependencies.
- Adjust int8 heuristics: factor in measured kernel-launch overhead from quantized kernels when evaluating tradeoffs.
- Add CI microbench: add synthetic tests covering 128..512 token ranges and assert p95 doesn't regress more than 20% when switching kernels. Run these at merge time for serving-runtime changes.

Longer-term ideas:
- Continuous profiling-based thresholds: collect real allocation footprints per model and compute thresholds per-model-version rather than global constants. Store per-model telemetry and use it as a prior for selection decisions.
- Soft blending: for requests close to switchpoint, run a micro-benchmark in adaptive mode (sample a small percentage of requests using the other kernel) and pick winner dynamically. This avoids a static threshold and learns actual tradeoffs under current load.
- Kernel fusion tuning pass: allow the compiler to emit fused kernels with optional paged-aware tiling so fusion and paging cooperate instead of fighting.

Action items / TODOs:
- [P1] Implement hysteresis and telemetry events (owner: Priya). Target: ship in patch release 2026-02-xx. Jira: INF-2721.
- [P2] Open PR to remove sync points in paged path and replace with stream/events (owner: Diego). Linked PR: runtime#859.
- [P3] Add CI microbench and guard band tests (owner: Maya).
- [P4] Run a full fleet rollout to 5% traffic after patch and monitor p95 for rw-large-7B and chat workloads.

Unresolved questions:
- How often do real production request patterns sit in the boundary region across tenants? We need customer telemetry to estimate exposure.
- Is there any case where paged-attention reduces latency despite higher kernel-launch overhead (e.g., memory-locality for very long contexts)? Need more multi-GPU tests.

Appendix: quick dumps of notable runs (trimmed)
- a100|rw-large-7B|fp16|batch=4|seq=380 -> Flash chosen, p95 34ms, avg kernel_time 22ms
- a100|rw-large-7B|fp16|batch=4|seq=392 -> Paged chosen, p95 78ms, avg kernel_time 64ms, extra_sync=9ms
- h100|rw-large-7B|int8|batch=2|seq=360 -> Flash chosen, p95 28ms, int8_launch_overhead 5ms

Notes to self: capture more H100 runs (especially for quant modes). Add a small sample profiler on production canary to capture allocated sizes per request. Link traces in confluence page once P1 is in.

End of doc.
